program: Free medical-legal assistance, disability benefits advocacy and health-access policy

what: Legal Council for Health Justice provides free legal help to people facing disability, HIV, homelessness and barriers to care.
Attorneys and advocates embedded in health and social-service settings help clients obtain benefits, resolve insurance disputes and secure educational supports.
Its benefits advocacy and coordinated referrals aim to improve income security and access to essential services.
strengths: Medical-legal partnerships reach people who may not independently find legal assistance.
Disability benefits advocacy has a concrete income-security mechanism and documented historical awards.
Current individual-client reporting and original returns support recipient identity and annual cost checks.
reservations: Current benefits awarded, unique households and counterfactual success were not reported quantitatively.
Clinical utility remains a weak prior; external randomized MLP findings are mixed.
Federal transfers and fixed-budget displacement are not free social income; central outside incidence is incomplete.

sections.what: Legal Council for Health Justice, EIN 36-3563802, provides free civil legal assistance through Chicago-area medical and social-service partnerships. Its direct programs serve people with HIV, children with chronic conditions and disabilities, and unhoused people with severe health conditions. Statewide advocacy and IL Pride Connect are additional channels, not all attributed to Chicago. The official donation page embeds a Little Green Light form; the route is current but no checkout transaction was tested.
sections.monitoring: The new 2025 annual report states over 1,600 individual clients. N=1600 is a conservative numerical reference, not a precise count or deduplicated household cohort. The older 2024 report identifies 1,610 clients and a 17.7% Homeless Outreach Program share. The new report spans fiscal finance, calendar-year supporters and events after June 2025, including December legislation; it is not one clean fiscal outcome cohort. A .177 HOP share is explicitly judged transfer of the older mix. Current 47% zero income is not zero household consumption. Resource baseline must include support, benefits and usable in-kind resources, not divide by zero cash income. Cases, web visits, hotline hours and class-action coverage are not additional clinical outcomes.
sections.qualitative: The Houston randomized medical-legal partnership study reported lower stress and fewer emergency visits but higher anxiety and hospital visits. It does not provide a direct QALY estimate or establish this recipient's clinical effect. The initial .20 response, .04 utility and one-year morbidity area remain weak conditional priors, not calibrated expected value. One aggregate health area avoids adding stress, housing, insurance access and HIV mortality again. No ordinary survivor earnings are credited. Full exposed-cohort harm and negative utility cases allow adverse results. Statewide policy efforts involve coalitions, implementation and existing funding; historical wins and broad covered populations are not priced as fresh annual donor outcomes.
sections.cost:
Original FY 2025 Form 990 expense is $3,646,350. Schedule D restores $139,067 donated services; $15,151 direct event costs are separately netted, giving full gross recognized resources $3,800,568. The Schedule D audited expense reference $3,780,384 excludes $5,033 investment expense already in the tax expense; keeping tax expense restores investment once, not twice. FY 2024 gross resources are $3,829,595 and FY 2023 $3,690,934, using the same tax + donated services + netted event convention; mean $3,773,699. These are whole recipient costs, including advocacy and support, not a program-only denominator. Current full audit was not obtained from the official page in this bounded review; original return reconciliation is observed, not a substitute claim of fresh audit verification. Unrecognized pro bono/provider opportunity resources remain unknown, with additional nonoverlapping $100,000 stress and unknown-cost cases.

b=.4 is a judged annual funded-work response beyond substitute funding/capacity, not another donor haircut on demonstrated incremental outcomes. The full annual denominator is retained and b=1 is shown. N 1600 × .4 gives 640 exposed client units, with .2 clinical response yielding 128 people. .04 utility for one finite year, quarter-year delay, 3% discount and .95 metro share yield 4.828189 clinical QALYs. Clinical responders are a subset of the resource-exposed clients; full harms and process costs cover all 640. No verified next-gift capacity price exists.

A distinct benefits pathway uses 2015 native evidence: 74 successful awards among 115 represented HOP clients. This is historical uncontrolled approval, not current causal success. A judged .5 current-transfer factor and .5 incremental-versus-alternative-advocate factor yield .16087 additional awards among HOP exposure. 640 × .177 =113.28 HOP clients, giving 18.2233 additional award hypotheses. The observed 2026 SSI individual maximum $994/month is a ceiling, not this cohort's average; .8 payable/net-retention is judged for reductions, taxes, lost benefits, support replacement and actual usable resources. No SSDI average or backpayment is invented. One finite benefit year after .75-year delay is modeled; recurring annual costs in the two-year sensitivity are conservative assumptions, not observed application charges.

Successful households receive $9,542.40 net annual benefit; positive welfare overlap .5 and full incremental time/travel/process costs $100 produce $4,671.20 net. Each other HOP household loses $100 against a judged $6,000 consumption baseline; other program households lose $100 against $15,000. One client per distinct household and one welfare-equivalent person are reference judgments. Two-client aggregation halves households and jointly doubles both awards and burdens before one household log, assuming similarly situated clients share households; family welfare is not automatically added. Work and otherwise-paid medical gains default unknown-neutral at 0, not observed zero. Positive components are individually discounted for overlap; every negative component and cost stays full. .5 × households × discounted years × log(1 + joint net/baseline) produces 2.495719 resource equivalents, combining to 7.323908 and $5.189262 million per ten combined equivalents, not ten clinical QALYs.

Clinical-null preserves income and all client costs. Financial-only, no incremental awards, no resource gains, adverse, full unknown and true-zero controls are distinct. Federal benefit transfers are recipient resource gains, not net new national income. Matched full gross-transfer incidence allocates the same $11,928 gross annual award per additional recipient across 1000 distinct payer households at $60,000 resources, without positive-overlap attenuation. A fixed-budget displacement stress uses $6,000 counterparty resources instead; these are alternative incidence hypotheses, not verified taxpayer geography. These pathways use the same finite benefit horizon and timing. Clinical care/provider own-resource loss stress excludes clinical input costs already in annual cost. Central payer, provider and displacement incidence is unknown-neutral: the local partial headline is not complete world net benefit or a lower bound. Retail legal or medical prices and gross class-action benefits are excluded.
sections.funding: FY 2025 return reports government grants $1,861,127 and net assets $4,011,092; program service revenue $373,026 supports substantial existing partnerships. Government, foundation and provider funding may replace donations or constrain scope, but reserves and grant mix do not prove zero expansion. Free assistance, SSA self-application, SOAR/social-service advocates, other legal-aid organizations, healthcare navigation and existing insurance/public-benefit eligibility are relevant counterfactuals. Ask for current HOP unique applicants, decisions, award amounts, delays, replacement assistance, household consumption and process burdens. Also request restricted/unrestricted resources, a full current audit and a priced unfunded advocacy capacity proposal. Statewide laws, historical grants and already-funded public benefits do not establish next-dollar causality.

model.costScope: Whole annual gross recognized recipient resources; unrecognized inputs and marginal gift unknown.
model.geographicAttribution: .95 judged Chicago share; current direct-client residence not verified; statewide portfolio unknown.
model.formula: Health=N*b*a*u*discountedYears(T,clinicalDelay)−N*b*harm, then metroshare. Additional awards=N*b*hopShare*(74/115)*currentTransfer*incrementalAwardShare. Household cash=maxSSI*12*payableShare; each positive component overlap discounted, all negatives/costs full, joint net before .5*HH*discountedYears*log1p(net/consumption). Headline10*C/(clinical+income).
model.counterfactual: Self-application, other lawyers/SOAR and public/medical providers continue; marginal funding replacement unknown.
model.attribution: Current local clinical response/awards not causal observations. Annual funded-work response separated from outcome counterfactual.
model.uncertainty: Conditional reference, not calibrated expected value. Full social transfer incidence, complete portfolio and next gift remain unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Individual clients receive assistance; current awards/dollars absent. Historical2015 HOP74 awards/115 represented is an uncontrolled outcome anchor, not current causal effect. Cases/hotline/web/class-action coverage not health.

historicalAlphaModel.formula: Q_all=N*k*a*u*T*b; Q_MSA=Q_all*g; price10=10*C/Q_MSA if positive, otherwise null. FiniteT<=1year, no survival extrapolation or lifetime multiplier; undiscounted short-horizon illustration.
historicalAlphaModel.costScope: Whole-recipient resource-adjusted accounting envelope: FY ended June30,2024 Form990 PartIX expense3,709,603 + ScheduleD recognized donated services/use100,400 + PartVIII direct event costs19,592 =3,829,595. ScheduleD audited-expense reference3,810,003 restores donated services but not the PartVIII direct event amount. Published donated-resource values are not verified opportunity costs; unrecognized volunteer/partner inputs remain unknown. No program-only numerator.
historicalAlphaModel.geographicAttribution: Chicagoland medical and social provider partnerships; g=.95 assumed resident share within pinned 13-county Chicago MSA, not measured. Statewide advocacy benefits excluded from modeled direct-client pathway.
historicalAlphaModel.nativeOutcomes: Annual report 2024 p3 identifies 1,610 clients; p7 says individual clients. Legal assistance is not itself a QALY.
historicalAlphaModel.counterfactual: a represents incremental response beyond alternative services; b discounts replacement funding and capacity limits. Both are judgments, not observed causal estimates.
historicalAlphaModel.attribution: One aggregate morbidity/stress relief pathway among 20% incrementally helped clients, .04 utility for one year, 40% funding additionality; all judged. Money/benefits recovered, class-action coverage, family members and partner healthcare benefits are not independently added.
historicalAlphaModel.uncertainty: All conversion parameters are illustrative judgments without probabilities, calibration or recipient causal QALY evidence. Scenarios are not confidence intervals or exhaustive bounds. Benefits of rights and autonomy beyond health are unpriced. Costs are not comparable full economic resource costs.
sensitivity: Zero additionality yields zero benefit and no finite price.
Poor and favorable vary multiple unsupported assumptions; these are illustrative scenarios, not probabilistic bounds.
Cost changes scale price proportionally; benefit factors scale price inversely.
Other organizational pathways are not quantified; omitted benefits are not demonstrated zero.
A50%cost allowance tests missing resources; not calibrated or complete. Lower local share and net-harm stresses show additional downside; no probability weights.
